deployment.traceability_note: PRODUCTION DOES NOT YET CARRY THE QA FIXES. Earlier manifests recorded production as runtime-equivalent to the packaged commit; that was true while every commit since e199045 touched only scripts and documentation. It is no longer true. `git diff e199045 3a1abdb -- worker/` now reports two changed files (worker/index.js, worker/client.js), and the two bundle hashes above differ. The five QA findings and the two follow-up regressions are fixed, verified on the isolated test environment, and awaiting a production deploy. Production continues to serve the e199045 runtime until `npm run deploy:prod` is run.

isolated_test_environment.purpose: Technical review copy. Separate Cloudflare resources throughout; it never reaches production data.
isolated_test_environment.contents: 5 synthetic projects and 5 demonstration accounts. No live record is present.
isolated_test_environment.safety_note: scripts/check-deploy-target.sh is the single definition of what each environment looks like. It asserts the project name, D1 name and id, R2 bucket, both binding names and ALLOW_PLATFORM_AUTH="false", and explicitly forbids the other environment's database id and bucket. Both deploy scripts run it before building or uploading. Note that the production resource names are strict PREFIXES of the test ones, so every assertion anchors on the whole key = "value" line; a substring match would pass against either environment.

latest_deployment.label_note: Cloudflare stamped this deployment f36f7e9 because that was HEAD when it was uploaded; the fixes were still uncommitted at that moment and were committed immediately afterwards as 3a1abdb. The artifact is 3a1abdb's: rebuilding at 3a1abdb reproduces bundle_sha256 above byte for byte.

workbook_import.purpose: Reconcile a bi-weekly D&C workbook into the tracker without disturbing existing data.
stages: scripts/parse-workbook.mjs        read the .xlsx, emit normalised JSON (no database contact)
scripts/reconcile-workbook.mjs    match against the tracker, emit a report (read-only SELECTs)
scripts/apply-workbook-import.mjs generate SQL; execute only with --execute and an explicit --target
workbook_import.dependencies_added: none — the .xlsx reader is built on node:zlib and the zip central directory
workbook_import.dates_policy: Report dates are never derived. scripts/workbook/import-<date>.json states both explicitly and a run without them fails rather than guessing, because the workbook's own 'Previous Week Update' column was measured to be an unreliable roll-forward.
workbook_import.idempotence: Deterministic keys on the UNIQUE project_updates.source_key column, guarded UPDATEs, hash-guarded audit rows and a per-report app_meta run marker. Verified by executing the same file twice against production: the second run wrote 0 rows and left the database byte-size unchanged.
workbook_import.documentation: docs/WORKBOOK_IMPORT.md — the fortnightly runbook, including the pipeline in execution order, the mandatory backup and how to verify it, how to read the reconciliation report, and the rules that must not be relaxed.

production_data_state.note: The September 11 workbook import added 2 projects and 36 history rows. All 128 pre-existing history rows were preserved, including the one user-authored update. Pre-import backup taken and verified by restoring it; see backup_before_import below.
production_data_state.audit_trail_note: All 31 audit rows from the import are attributed to 'Workbook Import' and share the timestamp 2026-09-17 08:24:50 — one import run. The Wheeling Island status change records status: Active -> Complete in the same shape the application writes for a human edit.

backup_before_import.note: Held outside the repository. It contains password hashes, session records and every staff email address, and must never be committed.

session_policy.activity_rule: State-changing requests (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) extend a session. All GET/HEAD/OPTIONS reads do not, so no background refresh or poll can keep an idle session alive.

local_test_credentials.policy: No password literal exists anywhere in this package.
local_test_credentials.detail: pages-test/setup.sh generates a random 20-character password per run and prints it, or uses LOCAL_PASS when supplied. Local development accounts only; never production credentials and never to be reused on a deployment.

qa_findings.source: Mina Ramzy, sanitized review and re-test
qa_findings.verified_against: the deployed isolated test environment and its real D1 database
findings: DNC-001  monetary decimal precision on save — FIXED
DNC-002  invalid cost, date and status values accepted — FIXED (400, nothing partially written)
DNC-003  temporary-password users could read project data — FIXED (428 before any project payload)
DNC-004  double-clicked activity save created duplicate history — FIXED (one row, one audit entry)
DNC-005  Development save reported success then lost the values — FIXED (upsert; values survive refresh)
follow_up_regressions: Invalid money still cleared the saved amount through the BROWSER: the client converted unparseable text to null before sending, and null is a valid instruction to clear. The server validator never saw the text. moneyNumber() now distinguishes blank (clear) from invalid (refuse), and all three save paths refuse.

Temporary-password users could not reach the password form. Blocking /api/bootstrap — correct in itself — removed the only route the client had to that dialog, because it read must_change_password from the bootstrap payload. /api/session now reports it, and the client opens the dialog from there. The 428 restriction is unchanged.
qa_findings.note: Both follow-ups were server-correct but browser-broken, and were missed because verification stopped at the API. The suite now exercises the served client code as well.
